tasks.short: Use radiation safety measures and protection devices

steps.what: Check procedure-specific radiation safety needs and applicable protection measures
Apply radiation safety measures and protection devices and verify patient and staff safety

tasks.design: Keep procedure-specific checks and physical radiation protection with the technologist. {DOCS} supplies the approved local protocol, without replacing direct checks or introducing automatic clearance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Protection depends on the procedure, patient and room conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: No demonstrated change to this physical safety work is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Exceptions require local clinical and radiation-protection expertise.
tasks.human_edge: Notice an unsafe condition and stop the procedure.
tasks.altitude: Safety responsibilities and decision rights remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Retaining radiation safety checks and physical protection in full is an E1 design judgement, without a saving claim.

assumptions: Boundary is safety assessment and applying protection, separate from image acquisition and exposure decisions.
No structured safety-clearance input or automated decision is introduced; technologist assessment remains counted in s1.
No software change or new upkeep is proposed, so native configuration is unnecessary.
unknowns: Local protection protocol, procedure mix and authorised responsibilities
research_questions: Which exceptions require immediate radiation-protection specialist review?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, upkeep=0 and net=0. No assumed paperwork replaces physical protection.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Operate digital picture archiving communications systems

steps.what: Verify patient and study identity before accessing the picture archive
Navigate archive screens and retrieve selected study images and prior examinations
Verify image completeness and archive status and resolve mismatched or missing studies

tasks.design: Configure native worklist links and saved retrieval views in the picture archive in {OTHER}. Reduce repeated navigation while retaining patient selection, image checks and exception resolution; existing automatic storage earns no new labour saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Technologists may repeat searches and screen navigation to open a study and its priors.
tasks.enabler_now: Native worklist context and saved views may reuse verified study references.
tasks.still_hard: Duplicate patient identities and incomplete transfers need direct investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise a wrong-patient or incomplete study before relying on it.
tasks.altitude: Less screen navigation; responsibility for archive verification stays unchanged.

evidence.claim: Native archive worklist links and the proposed navigation saving are E1 assumptions, not measured imaging-archive results.

assumptions: Boundary is technologist archive operation, excluding image acquisition and radiologist interpretation. OTHER is the picture archive category.

Existing registration and ordering staff produce patient reference and accession reference in the worklist; the scanner produces image identifiers and transfer status during existing acquisition. No new upstream capture is requested. Technologist verifies and selects patient and study in s1, retaining all 35 hours.
Retained s2 time includes confirming retrieval context and manual search when references or prior links are missing. No inferred identity matching is allowed.
Test native saved views first. Only changed navigation loses time; existing storage or retrieval runtime earns none. Three focal hours fund view and access upkeep.
unknowns: Current navigation effort and native worklist support
research_questions: Can saved views halve navigation without reducing patient selection or completeness checks?

already_counted.description: Retrieval-context review and manual search fallback

incremental.description: Maintain views, links and access checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=85, gross=15 minus 3 upkeep gives net=12. High assumes repeated manual navigation; low assumes only 3 navigation hours removable. Identity and archive verification retain 70 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take thorough and accurate patient medical histories

steps.what: Interview patient, clarify medical histories and check procedure-relevant details
Record and verify clarified history facts in the clinical record

tasks.design: Configure a native history-entry template in the clinical record in {OTHER} to reduce repeated labels and navigation. Keep all patient questioning and clarification, then have the technologist verify and file the exact history; no safety answer is copied forward as current without confirmation.
tasks.previous_blocker: History entry may require repeated labels and navigation after the interview.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates can group the required fields and reuse structure, not unconfirmed clinical answers.
tasks.still_hard: Uncertain medication, allergies or previous procedures need clarification.
tasks.human_edge: Ask sensitive questions in a way that helps the patient give an accurate account.
tasks.altitude: A small entry reduction leaves the clinical conversation intact.

reach.learn: Safe escalation and provenance of patient-reported facts

evidence.claim: A native history-entry template and six-hour gross saving are E1 design assumptions; consultation-scribe cases do not establish this template's results.

assumptions: Boundary is history interview and documentation, not subsequent protocol selection or exposure clearance. OTHER means the clinical record system.

Technologist produces each history answer, uncertainty, source and confirmation date during s1, with all 85 hours retained; entry and verification occur in s2. No structured allergy or contraindication flag is assumed to exist without this capture.
Blank or conflicting fields require manual clarification within retained interview and entry time. Template defaults never answer a clinical question.
Native templates come first. Two focal upkeep hours cover approved field and access changes.
unknowns: Required history fields and current entry layout
Who can verify and file the history
research_questions: Can grouped fields reduce entry by 40% after verification while interview duration remains unchanged?

already_counted.description: History entry, verification and filing approval

approvals.approved_version: Final history entry with patient reference, every answer, uncertainty, source and confirmation date; changes void approval before filing

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=94, gross=6 minus 2 upkeep gives net=4. High assumes repetitive labels and navigation; low assumes only 2 entry hours saved. All 85 interview hours remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Make exposures and reject or repeat substandard images

steps.what: Make exposures necessary for the requested procedure under authorised local protocol
Assess image standards and decide whether to accept, reject or repeat exposures

tasks.design: Keep exposure and repeat decisions with the authorised technologist at the imaging console in {OTHER}. The digest's image measurement tools do not establish that exposure or quality acceptance can lose human time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Image adequacy and repeat exposure involve patient-specific judgement and physical action.
tasks.enabler_now: No demonstrated change to this task is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Motion, positioning and dose trade-offs must be judged for each procedure.
tasks.human_edge: Avoid an unnecessary repeat while recognising when images cannot answer the request.
tasks.altitude: Exposure and acceptance authority remains unchanged.

reach.learn: When an uncertain quality decision needs review

evidence.claim: Siemens AI-Rad Companion measures nodules and brain volumes; that capability does not establish autonomous exposure or repeat decisions.
Retaining all exposure and quality-decision time is an E1 task design.

assumptions: Boundary includes acquisition and quality/repeat decisions, excluding separately modelled radiation protection and archive administration. Repeated acquisition cycles are included in the 60-hour acquisition share.
OTHER is the imaging console category. Technologist produces acquisition settings and quality observations during the retained steps; no structured acceptability flag is assumed.
No new software or upkeep is proposed; existing console runtime earns no labour saving and native configuration is unnecessary.
unknowns: Local authorisation, image standards and escalation rules
research_questions: Which quality failures require radiologist review before another exposure?

already_counted.description: Acquisition and quality decisions retained in full

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, upkeep=0 and net=0. Existing scanner automation and image measurement capabilities earn no new saving here.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Some archive navigation and history-entry effort may shrink; radiation safety, patient questioning and exposure judgement remain central.
reach: Radiologist: image adequacy and protocol exceptions
Medical records specialist: safe identity correction
role.ambitious_version: Maintain reliable patient-linked imaging records while preserving direct clinical responsibility for protection and exposures.
